s:
Consider the following statements about Neelam Sanjiva Reddy:
1. As the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh he appointed no Deputy Chief Minister, calling the post a "sixth finger".
2. He became Chief Minister again in March 1962, succeeding Damodaram Sanjivayya.
3. He resigned in 1964 to join Jawaharlal Nehru's cabinet as a Union Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: after the Kurnool bus-routes verdict he resigned in 1964 and joined Lal Bahadur Shastri's (not Nehru's) cabinet as Union Minister of Steel and Mines.

s:
Consider the following statements about P.V. Narasimha Rao as Chief Minister:
1. He was Chief Minister during the Jai Andhra movement of 1972.
2. The Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act was passed by his ministry in 1975.
3. He was the Chief Minister immediately before President's Rule was imposed on 18 January 1973.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct (CM 30 Sep 1971 – Jan 1973; Jai Andhra 1972 led to President's Rule on 18 Jan 1973). Statement 2 is wrong: the Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act is of 1973, not 1975.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Chief Minister)
a. N.T. Rama Rao
b. N. Chandrababu Naidu
c. Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy
d. Nadendla Bhaskara Rao
List-II (Distinction)
1. Longest continuous tenure in united AP
2. First non-Congress CM
3. Shortest tenure – 31 days
4. First CM from the Legislative Council
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: NTR (1983) was the first non-Congress CM; Chandrababu Naidu (1995–2004) had the longest continuous tenure in united AP; Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy (1982) was the first CM from the Legislative Council; Nadendla Bhaskara Rao (16 Aug – 16 Sep 1984) had the shortest tenure, 31 days.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Chief Ministers of 2009–2014:
1. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy died in a helicopter crash in the Nallamala forest on 2 September 2009.
2. N. Kiran Kumar Reddy succeeded Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy on 3 September 2009.
3. N. Kiran Kumar Reddy was the last Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: K. Rosaiah succeeded YSR on 3 Sep 2009; Kiran Kumar Reddy became CM on 25 Nov 2010 and was the last CM of united AP.

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh after 2014:
1. Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy was Chief Minister of residual Andhra Pradesh from 2019 to 2024.
2. In 2026, S. Abdul Nazeer is the Governor of Andhra Pradesh.
3. In 2026, Andhra Pradesh has two Deputy Chief Ministers, one of them K. Pawan Kalyan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: K. Pawan Kalyan is the sole Deputy CM in 2026 (Jagan's 2019–24 cabinet had five Deputy CMs).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Telugu Desam Party:
1. N.T. Rama Rao founded it on 29 March 1982, when T. Anjaiah was Chief Minister.
2. It won 202 seats in the 1983 Assembly election.
3. Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was Deputy Chief Minister in NTR's first cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the TDP was founded on 29 March 1982 when Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy, not Anjaiah, was CM.

s:
Consider the following statements about the measures of N.T. Rama Rao's government:
1. The Rs 2 per kg rice scheme began on 14 April 1983.
2. A Women's University was set up at Tirupati.
3. The Mandal system of local administration was introduced in 1985.
4. The Legislative Council was revived in 1985.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: NTR abolished the Legislative Council in 1985; it was revived only in 2007.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Party)
a. Telugu Desam Party (1982)
b. Democratic Telugu Desam Party (1984)
c. National Democratic Party (1984)
d. Swatantra Party in AP (1959)
List-II (Leader)
1. Nadendla Bhaskara Rao
2. N.G. Ranga
3. Marri Chenna Reddy
4. N.T. Rama Rao
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: TDP – NTR; Democratic Telugu Desam Party – Nadendla Bhaskara Rao; National Democratic Party – Marri Chenna Reddy (both 1984 breakaways); Swatantra Party (1959) – N.G. Ranga.

s:
Consider the following statements about Panchayat Raj in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was introduced in Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1959.
2. Andhra Pradesh was the first State to introduce it, ahead of Rajasthan.
3. It was introduced when Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was Chief Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Rajasthan was first (2 October 1959); AP followed on 1 November 1959.

s:
Consider the following statements about politics and institutions of united Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Congress won 177 seats in the 1962 Assembly election.
2. After the Congress (I) was formed on 1 January 1978, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy led the rival Reddy Congress.
3. OCTOPUS (2007) is the anti-Naxal force of AP, while the Greyhounds is its anti-terror commando force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 swaps the roles: OCTOPUS (2007) is the anti-terror commando force; the Greyhounds is the anti-Naxal force.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Leader)
a. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
b. Damodaram Sanjivayya
c. P.V. Narasimha Rao
d. Nadendla Manohar
List-II (Office / distinction)
1. Last Speaker of combined AP
2. First (and only) Prime Minister from AP
3. AICC President 1960, Lok Sabha Speaker, President of India 1977
4. AICC President and first Dalit CM in India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: N. Sanjiva Reddy – AICC President 1960, Lok Sabha Speaker, President of India 1977; Sanjivayya – first Dalit CM, later AICC President; P.V. Narasimha Rao – only PM from AP; Nadendla Manohar – last Speaker of combined AP (2011–14).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The dismissal of N.T. Rama Rao's government by Governor Ram Lal in August 1984 is cited as a classic misuse of the Governor's discretion.
Reason (R): The 1984 crisis fed into the 52nd Amendment (1985), the anti-defection law.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true: NTR was dismissed in Aug 1984, Nadendla was made CM and NTR was restored on 16 Sep 1984; the crisis fed the 52nd Amendment (1985). But R is a later consequence, not the reason why the dismissal is called a misuse of discretion.

s:
Consider the following statements about the formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1956:
1. It joined the 11 districts of Andhra State with 9 Telugu districts of Hyderabad State.
2. The draft Bill named the State "Andhra Telangana"; the Communists wanted "Visalandhra"; the Joint Select Committee chose "Andhra Pradesh".
3. The Andhra Legislature, meeting at Kurnool, backed the merger by a narrow majority.
4. Hyderabad was made the capital in view of the SRC's opinion and the Mahasabha demand.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Andhra Legislature at Kurnool backed the merger unanimously.

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra State (1953–56):
1. Its capital was Kurnool and its first Chief Minister was Bezawada Gopala Reddy.
2. Prakasam's ministry fell on the issue of prohibition in 1954.
3. Bezawada Gopala Reddy became CM after the 1955 mid-term polls.
4. The Wanchoo Committee award fixed the Andhra–Madras border and gave Tiruttani to Tamil Nadu.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first CM of Andhra State (capital Kurnool) was Tanguturi Prakasam, with N. Sanjiva Reddy as Deputy CM; Bezawada Gopala Reddy came after the 1955 polls. Statement 4 is wrong: the border was fixed by the Pataskar Award; the Wanchoo Committee (Dec 1952) only identified the financial and administrative problems of forming Andhra State.

s:

List-I (Office in AP (first holder))
a. Deputy Speaker
b. Leader of Opposition
c. Chairman, Legislative Council (1958)
d. Deputy Chief Minister
List-II (Person)
1. Madapati Hanumantha Rao
2. K.V. Ranga Reddy
3. Kalluri Subbarao
4. Puchalapalli Sundarayya
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: First Deputy Speaker – Kalluri Subbarao; first Leader of Opposition – Puchalapalli Sundarayya; first Council Chairman – Madapati Hanumantha Rao; first Deputy CM – K.V. Ranga Reddy (1959–62).

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Minister (first AP ministry, 1956))
a. Bezawada Gopala Reddy
b. K.V. Ranga Reddy
c. Kasu Brahmananda Reddy

1. Irrigation and Electricity
2. Local Bodies
3. Finance
4. Home
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: In the first ministry Bezawada Gopala Reddy held Finance, K.V. Ranga Reddy Home, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy Local Bodies and J.V. Narsing Rao Irrigation and Electricity (D. Sanjivayya – Labour).

s:
Consider the following statements about the early legislature of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Congress strength in the new Assembly was 159 (40 from Hyderabad + 119 from Andhra).
2. The 1957 elections were held only in Telangana, for 79 seats.
3. The Legislative Council was set up in 1958 with 90 members and abolished by N.T. Rama Rao in 1985.
4. The Legislative Council was revived in 2004.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1–3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Council was revived in 2007 (YSR), again with 90 members.

s:
Consider the following statements about the roots of the Visalandhra idea:
1. In 1912 Unnava Lakshminarayana and Jonnavittula Gurunatham sketched a united Andhra.
2. At the second Andhra Mahasabha (1914) Nyapati Subbarao proposed one rule for all Telugu areas.
3. The Andhra Congress Swaraj Party manifesto of 1946 is one of its roots.
4. In 1954 Madapati Hanumantha Rao said the idea was 50 years old.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Andhra Congress Swaraj Party manifesto was of 1936, not 1946 (1946 is when the Communists began demanding integrated linguistic states).

s:
Consider the following statements about Puchalapalli Sundarayya and Visalandhra:
1. He coined the word 'Visalandhra' and wrote Visalandhralo Prajarajyam.
2. The Communist daily 'Visalandhra' was started in June 1949.
3. He later became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the daily Visalandhra began in June 1952 (1949 is the year of the Visalandhra Mahasabha).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Communists and the Visalandhra campaign:
1. The Hyderabad State Communist Party was practically a branch of the Andhra party, whose headquarters was Vijayawada.
2. Its 1952 electoral front in Hyderabad State was the People's Democratic Front.
3. The Congress welcomed Visalandhra at once because the idea came from the Communists.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Congress was at first cold to Visalandhra precisely because the idea came from the Communists.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Visalandhra resolutions of 1950–54:
1. The APCC resolution of January 1950 wanted Madras as the temporary and Hyderabad as the permanent capital.
2. In June 1953 the Hyderabad Congress proposed splitting Hyderabad State into Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and United Karnataka.
3. The Socialists, meeting at Kurnool in March 1954, opposed Visalandhra.
4. The first Visalandhra Mahasabha session at Warangal wanted Secunderabad as the capital.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong – the Socialists at Kurnool (21–22 Mar 1954) were for Visalandhra; statement 4 is wrong – the Warangal session (Feb 1950) wanted Hyderabad as capital.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Meeting)
a. Founding of the Visalandhra Mahasabha, Vijayawada (1949)
b. First Mahasabha session, Warangal (1950)
c. Second Mahasabha, Hyderabad (1954)
d. First meeting of the Andhra Jana Sangham, Hyderabad (1922)
List-II (Presided by)
1. Hayagreevachari
2. Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
3. K.V. Ranga Reddy
4. Sri Sri
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Kaleswara Rao founded and presided over the Mahasabha (Vijayawada, 26 Nov 1949); Hayagreevachari presided at Warangal (1950); Sri Sri at Hyderabad (1954); K.V. Ranga Reddy presided over the first Andhra Jana Sangham meeting (14 Feb 1922).

s:
Consider the following statements about Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao:
1. He raised the Visalandhra demand at the 1951 Bangalore Congress manifesto meeting.
2. He translated Jawaharlal Nehru's Vijayawada speech into Telugu.
3. He was the first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the speech he translated at Vijayawada was Mahatma Gandhi's.

s:

a. The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh
b. Enni Naalla Swapnamidi
c. Emaanandam ... Eenadu
d. Imroz
List-II (Author / editor)
1. Shoebullah Khan
2. Kaloji
3. Dasarathi
4. K.V. Narayana Rao
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh – K.V. Narayana Rao; 'Enni Naalla Swapnamidi' – Dasarathi; 'Emaanandam ... Eenadu' – Kaloji; Imroz – Shoebullah Khan (Rayyat – Mandumula Narsing Rao).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. It was signed at Hyderabad House, New Delhi.
2. It was modelled on the Lucknow Pact.
3. It was signed by eight leaders, four each from Andhra and Telangana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct (20 Feb 1956, 4 + 4 signatories). Statement 2 is wrong: it followed the model of the Sribagh Pact (1937).

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Signatory)
a. Gouthu Latchanna
b. J.V. Narsing Rao
c. K.V. Ranga Reddy
d. Bezawada Gopala Reddy
List-II (Post held in 1956)
1. Minister, Andhra State
2. CM, Andhra State
3. President, Hyderabad PCC
4. Deputy CM, Hyderabad
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Gouthu Latchanna signed as a Minister of Andhra State, J.V. Narsing Rao as Hyderabad PCC President, K.V. Ranga Reddy as Deputy CM of Hyderabad and Bezawada Gopala Reddy as CM of Andhra State.

s:
Consider the following statements about the safeguards of the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. Telangana's revenue surplus was to be spent only on Telangana, with a review after five years.
2. Telangana students were assured at least one-third of the seats in technical institutions.
3. Recruitment in Telangana required 15 years' residence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the domicile condition was 12 years' residence (15 years was the Nizam's Mulki rule).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. Urdu was to continue for five years.
2. The sale of agricultural land in Telangana was to be controlled by the Regional Council.
3. At least one Muslim minister was to be from Telangana.
4. The Chief Minister and the Deputy Chief Minister were to be from different regions.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: All four are correct: Urdu for five years, land sales controlled by the Regional Council, at least one Muslim minister from Telangana, and CM and Deputy CM from different regions.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. The portfolios of Home and Finance were reserved for Telangana.
2. A statutory Regional Council of 20 members was to work for Telangana's development, its working to be reviewed after ten years.
3. Retrenchment in services was to be proportionate and recruitment by population ratio.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Telangana was to get at least two of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning & Development and Commerce & Industry – Home and Finance were not reserved.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana Regional Committee:
1. It rested on Article 371(1) and the AP Regional Committee Order, 1958.
2. Its first Chairman was K. Achyuta Reddy, MLA from Kodangal.
3. In 1968 it was extended by ten years.
4. It was wound up after the 32nd Amendment (1973).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Committee was extended by five years in 1968.

s:
Consider the following statements about the legal legacy of the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. Article 371D was inserted by the 32nd Amendment (1973), giving effect to the Six-Point Formula.
2. The Presidential Order of 1975 set up the Telangana Regional Committee.
3. Section 97 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended Article 371D to the State of AP or the State of Telangana.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Presidential Order of 1975 organised local cadres and regulated direct recruitment; the Regional Committee came from Art 371(1) and the 1958 Order and was wound up after the 32nd Amendment.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Violations of the Gentlemen's Agreement over jobs, domicile and surplus funds led to the Jai Telangana agitation of 1969.
Reason (R): The Gentlemen's Agreement contained no domicile condition for recruitment in Telangana.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: A is true: violations over jobs, domicile and surplus funds led to the 1969 agitation. R is false: the Agreement laid down 12 years' residence for recruitment in Telangana.

s:
Consider the following statements about Hyderabad State before 1956:
1. The Andhra Jana Sangham (1921) grew into the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha.
2. The first session of the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha was held at Jogipet in 1930, presided by Suravaram Pratapa Reddy.
3. Swami Ramananda Tirtha launched the "Join Indian Union" movement on 15 August 1947.
4. Hyderabad was integrated with India by Operation Polo on 17 September 1948.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Join Indian Union movement was launched on 7 August 1947.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mulki question in Hyderabad State:
1. The Mulki rules originated with the Nizam's farman of 1919.
2. The Mulki agitation of 1952 took place under Burgula Ramakrishna Rao's ministry and saw police firing near City College, Hyderabad.
3. The firing was inquired into by Justice Pingali Jaganmohan Reddy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Mulki rules date from 1888; the 1919 farman only tightened them.

s:
Consider the following statements about the States Reorganisation Commission and Hyderabad:
1. Its members were Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar.
2. On 8 July 1954 a Hyderabad PCC delegation asked it for a self-sufficient Telangana of 9 districts with Bastar and parts of Chanda.
3. Under para 386, Telangana could merge with Andhra after the 1961 elections if a simple majority of its legislature agreed.
4. It recommended that Raichur and Gulbarga go to Mysore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: para 386 required a two-thirds majority of the Telangana legislature after the 1961 elections.

s:
Consider the following statements about the merger votes of 1955–56:
1. In the Hyderabad Assembly, 103 members voted for Visalandhra, 29 against and 15 stayed neutral.
2. The Andhra Assembly passed Bezawada Gopala Reddy's merger resolution of 1955 by a two-thirds majority.
3. In 1956 the Congress leadership called the leaders of both regions to Delhi to settle their differences.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Andhra Assembly passed the resolution unanimously.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Leader / party)
a. Swami Ramananda Tirtha
b. Tanguturi Prakasam
c. Hyderabad PSP (Mahadev Singh)
d. C. Rajagopalachari (1949)
List-II (Stand on Visalandhra)
1. Wanted a separate Telangana
2. Wanted Hyderabad kept multilingual
3. A separate Telangana would be weak and democratic forces suppressed
4. "Visalandhra nirmanam is the mother's right of all Andhras"
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Ramananda Tirtha backed Visalandhra, warning a separate Telangana would be weak; Prakasam called it the mother's right of all Andhras; the Hyderabad PSP under Mahadev Singh wanted a separate Telangana; Rajagopalachari (1949) wanted a multilingual Hyderabad.

s:
Consider the following statements about the leaders' stands on Visalandhra:
1. Marri Chenna Reddy opposed Visalandhra throughout.
2. Harishchandra Heda backed a separate Telangana in November 1955.
3. Burgula, Mandumula Narsing Rao and Pandit Narendraji were against Visalandhra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, Mandumula Narsing Rao and Pandit Narendraji supported Visalandhra.

s:
Consider the following statements about the merger debate:
1. Integrated planning of the Krishna and Godavari was an argument for Visalandhra.
2. The Communists argued that unification would protect the old feudal landholdings.
3. Telangana feared a weakening of the Mulki rules and the spending of its revenue surplus elsewhere.
4. The SRC held that Hyderabad was unsuitable as a capital and a new capital would be needed.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Communists' agrarian argument was that unification would push land reform and weaken feudalism. Statement 4 is wrong: the SRC's case for Visalandhra counted Hyderabad as a ready capital.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Telangana leaders argued that Telangana was viable as a separate State.
Reason (R): Telangana had a higher per capita income and revenue than Andhra State.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true and R explains A: Telangana's higher per capita income and revenue were the basis of the claim that it could exist alone.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. It has 12 Parts, 108 Sections and 13 Schedules.
2. It fixes the population ratio of AP and Telangana at 58.32 : 41.68 on the basis of the 2011 Census.
3. It was passed with the consent of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (Act 6 of 2014; Sec 2(h)). Statement 3 is wrong: a major criticism is that it was passed without the AP Assembly's consent.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Part of APRA 2014)
a. Part II
b. Part IV
c. Part IX
d. Part XII
List-II (Subject)
1. High Court
2. Legal and Miscellaneous – amends Articles 168 and 371D
3. Reorganisation of the State – Telangana, common capital, Governor
4. Management and Development of Water Resources
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Part II (Secs 3–11) – reorganisation of the State; Part IV (30–43) – High Court; Part IX (84–91) – water resources; Part XII (96–108) – legal and miscellaneous, amending Art 168 (Sec 96, Telangana's Council) and Art 371D (Sec 97).

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Section of APRA 2014)
a. Section 10
b. Section 26
c. Section 46
d. Section 90
List-II (Subject)
1. Polavaram declared a national project
2. Finance Commission award split and backward-area package
3. First Schedule entry "29. Telangana"
4. Assembly seats to rise 175 → 225 (AP) and 119 → 153 (Telangana)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Sec 10 – First Schedule entry 29, Telangana; Sec 26 – delimitation, AP 175 → 225 and Telangana 119 → 153 (subject to Art 170, not yet done); Sec 46 – Finance Commission award and backward-area package; Sec 90 – Polavaram a national project.

s:
Consider the following statements about the provisions of APRA 2014:
1. Under Section 30 the common High Court sat at Hyderabad.
2. Under Section 50 arrears of taxes other than property tax go by the place of assessment.
3. Under Section 82 employees of State PSUs continue in their posts for one year.
4. Under Section 108 an order removing difficulties can be made at any time, with no time limit.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1–3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: no order under Sec 108 can be made after three years from the appointed day.

s:
Consider the following statements about APRA 2014:
1. Sections 84–85 provide for the Apex Council and the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards.
2. Under Section 95 the existing admission quotas under Article 371D continue for five years.
3. Under Section 93 the Thirteenth Schedule measures are to be taken within ten years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Sec 95 continues the Art 371D admission quotas for 10 years.

s:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the AP Reorganisation Bill:
1. The Group of Ministers on bifurcation (Oct 2013) was headed by Home Minister Sushil Kumar Shinde.
2. The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 18 February 2014 and the Rajya Sabha on 20 February 2014.
3. The President gave assent on 2 June 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: assent came on 1 March 2014; 2 June 2014 was the appointed day on which Telangana was formed.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (House (after 2014))
a. Lok Sabha seats of AP
b. Rajya Sabha seats of Telangana
c. Assembly seats of Telangana
d. Legislative Council of Telangana
List-II (Seats)
1. 40
2. 7
3. 25
4. 119
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: AP got 25 Lok Sabha and 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 175 Assembly seats and a 58-member Council; Telangana got 17 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha, 119 Assembly and 40 Council seats.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Item apportioned)
a. Assets
b. Liabilities and public debt
c. Tax arrears
d. Power
List-II (Basis under APRA 2014)
1. Average consumption of the previous 5 years
2. Location
3. Place of assessment
4. Population ratio
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Assets go by location; liabilities, public debt and refunds by population ratio (so AP, with 58%, carries more debt); tax arrears by place of assessment; power by average consumption of the previous five years.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Residuary Andhra Pradesh faced revenue deficits after the bifurcation.

Consider the following statements about the Jai Andhra movement (1972–73):
1. It was led by Kakani Venkataratnam and Marri Chenna Reddy.
2. Its main issue was that Andhras were treated as "outsiders" in Hyderabad, a capital built with the whole State's revenue.
3. Tenneti Viswanatham was among its leaders, and students formed its core.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: its leaders were Kakani Venkataratnam, B.V. Subba Reddy and Tenneti Viswanatham; Marri Chenna Reddy led the 1969 Telangana Praja Samithi.

Consider the following statements about the Five-Point Formula of 1972:
1. It was announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on 27 November 1972.
2. The Mulki rules were to continue in the twin cities till 1980 and in the rest of Telangana till 1977.
3. One in three Secretariat posts was to go to Telangana locals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 reverses the years: Mulki rules were to continue in the twin cities till 1977 and in Telangana till 1980.

1. A separate Andhra flag was hoisted on 10 December 1972.
2. President's Rule from 18 January to 10 December 1973 was the first in the State.
3. The agitation was called off on 1 October 1973.
4. Kasu Brahmananda Reddy became Chief Minister when President's Rule ended.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1–3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Jalagam Vengala Rao became CM on 10 Dec 1973 after the ~11-month President's Rule.

Consider the following statements about the Six-Point Formula and the 32nd Amendment:
1. The Six-Point Formula, given on 21 September 1973, was approved on 18 December 1973.
2. The Mulki Rules were replaced by the zonal system.
3. The 32nd Amendment came into force on 1 July 1974.
4. The 32nd Amendment inserted Article 371D, while Article 371E was added by the 33rd Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1–3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the 32nd Amendment Act (1973) inserted both 371D and 371E; '33rd' was only the Bill's number.

1. Amaravati was chosen in 2015 and about 33,000 acres were pooled for it.
2. On 3 March 2022 the AP High Court upheld the three-capitals plan.
3. The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 made Amaravati the sole, permanent capital with effect from 2 June 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the High Court on 3 March 2022 upheld Amaravati and the three-capitals plan failed. Hyderabad's joint-capital term ended in June 2024.

1. Polavaram was first proposed as Ramapada Sagaram by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
2. The Apex Council for the Krishna and Godavari waters is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
3. Telangana says the Polavaram–Banakacherla link violates APRA and the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal Award.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong – the Apex Council is chaired by the Union Water Resources Minister with both CMs; statement 3 is wrong – Telangana cites the Godavari (GWDT) Award of 1980.

Consider the following statements about Articles 2 to 4 of the Constitution:
1. Article 2 deals with the admission or establishment of new States from outside India.
2. A law made under Article 3 is deemed an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
3. A Bill under Article 3 can be introduced only on the President's recommendation and is passed by a simple majority.
4. The time limit for the State legislature to give its views was added by the 5th Amendment, 1955.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 4 says such a law is not an amendment under Article 368.

2. Under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, Chandigarh became a Union Territory and the shared capital.
3. Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Goa became States in 1987.

x: Statements 1–3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Chhattisgarh came first (1 Nov 2000), then Uttarakhand (9 Nov) and Jharkhand (15 Nov).

Consider the following statements about the Mulki rules:
1. Under the 1888 rules an outsider could get a State post only with the Prime Minister's (Diwan's) permission.
2. The 1919 Nizam's Farman required the Nizam's personal permission.
3. Under the Nizam's rules a Mulki needed 12 years' continuous residence.
4. The Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act was passed in 1957.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Nizam's rules required 15 years; 12 years was the Gentlemen's Agreement condition.

Consider the following statements about the Telangana agitation of 1969:
1. It began as a student strike at Khammam in January 1969.
2. The first hunger strike was by the student Ravindranath.
3. Police firings killed about 36 people.
4. Its ideologue, Prof. K. Jayashankar, was a former Vice-Chancellor of Osmania University.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong – police firings killed over 360 (the Telangana martyrs); statement 4 is wrong – Jayashankar was a former VC of Kakatiya University.

1. It was formed in February 1969 with A. Madan Mohan as convener.
2. Its symbol was the spade.
3. It won 10 of the 14 Lok Sabha seats in 1971 and merged with the Congress in September 1971 after an agreement with Indira Gandhi.
4. Opponents of the merger formed the Complete TPS under Prof. K. Jayashankar.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1–3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Complete TPS was formed under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.
